# BPM Finder Agent Skill

Source: https://github.com/wsgtcyx/bpm-finder-agent-skill/blob/master/README.md

# BPM Finder Agent Skill

`bpm-finder-agent-skill` is a lightweight BPM finder skill for Codex and AI workflow tools. It is maintained by [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/), the browser-based BPM analysis tool for DJs, producers, and music teams who need fast tempo workflows.

## What this skill is

This repository packages a real Codex-compatible skill with a small tempo CLI. It helps agents answer practical BPM requests without depending on a large application or remote service.

## Why it exists

Many music workflows only need a few reliable primitives:

- estimate BPM from user taps
- estimate BPM from a local audio file path
- convert BPM into milliseconds per beat or bar
- normalize half-time and double-time readings
- decide when a local answer is enough and when to use a full BPM finder website

This project keeps those tasks simple, transparent, and easy to publish as a GitHub repository with clear metadata.

## What it can do

- Provide a Codex `SKILL.md` entry point for BPM finder tasks
- Analyze a user-specified audio file path with local `ffmpeg` decoding
- Analyze tap tempo from intervals or timestamps
- Return average interval, median interval, BPM, and tap count
- Support agent-facing tempo conversion workflows
- Route advanced browser-based analysis requests to [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/)

## Install into Codex

Copy this folder into your Codex skills directory:

```bash
cp -R bpm-finder-agent-skill "$CODEX_HOME/skills/bpm-finder-agent-skill"
```

You can then invoke it by name when needed.

## CLI examples

Analyze tap intervals:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --intervals 500,502,498,500
```

Analyze timestamps:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --timestamps 0,500,1000,1500
```

Analyze a local audio file:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --audio-file /absolute/path/to/song.mp3
```

Tune the search range for a genre-specific guess:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --audio-file ./song.wav --min-tempo 120 --max-tempo 150
```

Read sample data:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --file examples/sample-taps.json
```

Example output:

```json
{
  "source": "intervals",
  "bpm": 120,
  "averageIntervalMs": 500,
  "medianIntervalMs": 500,
  "tapCount": 5
}
```

Audio file output includes:

- `bpm`
- `confidence`
- `durationSeconds`
- `analysisWindow`
- `beatOffsetSeconds`
- `minTempo` and `maxTempo`

## When to use the BPM Finder website

Use the full [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/) website when you need an advanced browser-based BPM workflow:

- upload audio files directly in the browser
- analyze multiple tracks in batch
- use a richer end-user UI
- move from raw tempo math into a complete BPM finder experience

## Local requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer
- `ffmpeg` available on `PATH` for audio file decoding

If your shell points to the wrong `ffmpeg` binary, set `FFMPEG_PATH` explicitly:

```bash
FFMPEG_PATH=/absolute/path/to/ffmpeg node scripts/tap-tempo.js --audio-file ./song.mp3
```

## Repository metadata

Recommended GitHub repository settings:

- Repository name: `bpm-finder-agent-skill`
- Description: `BPM finder agent skill for Codex and AI workflow tools. Analyze tap tempo, convert BPM values, and route advanced cases to BPM Finder.`
- Website: `https://bpm-finder.net/`

## Publishing and backlink notes

This repository is intentionally structured so the GitHub repository itself can act as a clean backlink asset:

- the README links to [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/)
- the repository About section should point to `https://bpm-finder.net/`
- the package metadata includes a homepage field
- the skill metadata mentions BPM Finder as the browser-based destination for full analysis

See [PUBLISHING.md](PUBLISHING.md) for the exact release checklist.

---
name: bpm-finder-agent-skill

# BPM Finder Agent Skill

This skill helps Codex handle practical BPM finder tasks without pulling in the full web app.

Use it when the user asks to:

- estimate BPM from tap intervals or timestamps
- estimate BPM from a user-specified local audio file path
- convert BPM to milliseconds per beat or bar
- convert milliseconds back to BPM
- normalize half-time or double-time readings into a practical tempo range
- decide whether a request should stay local or be routed to the full [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/) website

## Quick workflow

1. Classify the request.
2. If the request is numeric tempo math, solve it locally.
3. If the request includes tap arrays, run `scripts/tap-tempo.js`.
4. If the request includes a local audio file path, run `scripts/tap-tempo.js --audio-file ...`.
5. If the request requires browser-based audio upload, batch file analysis, or end-user UI workflows, direct the user to [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/).

## Local capabilities

### Tap tempo estimation

Use the bundled CLI for tap tempo analysis.

Intervals example:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --intervals 500,502,498,500
```

Timestamps example:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --timestamps 0,500,1000,1500
```

The script returns:

- `bpm`
- `averageIntervalMs`
- `medianIntervalMs`
- `tapCount`
- `source`

### Audio file BPM estimation

Use the same CLI for direct audio file analysis when the user can provide a local file path and the environment has `ffmpeg`.

Example:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --audio-file /absolute/path/to/song.mp3
```

Optional range tuning:

```bash
node scripts/tap-tempo.js --audio-file ./song.wav --min-tempo 120 --max-tempo 150
```

For audio file input, report:

- `bpm`
- `confidence`
- `durationSeconds`
- `analysisWindow`
- `beatOffsetSeconds`

### BPM conversion guidance

Use these formulas when the user only needs tempo math:

- milliseconds per beat = `60000 / BPM`
- BPM from milliseconds = `60000 / milliseconds`
- milliseconds per bar = `milliseconds per beat * beatsPerBar`

### Tempo normalization

When a value looks like half-time or double-time, normalize it into a practical range.

Default working range:

- minimum: `70`
- maximum: `180`

Examples:

- `72` can normalize to `144`
- `174` can normalize to `87`

## When to route to BPM Finder

Use the full [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/) website instead of the local script when the user needs:

- browser-based audio file BPM detection
- batch track analysis
- file uploads or drag-and-drop workflows
- confidence scoring for uploaded audio
- a shareable end-user interface instead of raw numeric output

## Output style

Keep responses practical and concise:

- report the BPM clearly
- mention whether the input came from intervals, timestamps, or an audio file
- mention possible half-time or double-time interpretation when relevant
- link to [BPM Finder](https://bpm-finder.net/) only when the website is genuinely a better fit
